text: He said he'd call me later.
She told me to wait at the bar.
He asked if I was coming.
She said she'd already heard it.

Never believe a story from a party until you hear it from the person. Last month, my neighbor Frank told me that he was going to sell his boat. That was all. The next week, a man at the club asked me if Frank was moving to Portugal. His wife said she had heard that Frank had won the lottery. And at a birthday party on Saturday, a woman told me that Frank and his wife were getting divorced. So I called Frank. He laughed and said that he was only selling the boat because he wanted a bigger one. He asked me who had started the rumor. I told him I had no idea. Every person added one small detail, and nobody lied on purpose. That is how gossip works.

Some people say that gossip is always bad. I do not agree. Gossip is how a small town talks to itself. When my friend Laura was sick last winter, nobody told me directly. A woman at the bakery said that Laura had been in the hospital for a week. I called Laura that evening, and she told me she was fine but very tired. She asked me to bring her some soup, and I did. If the woman at the bakery had not talked, I would not have known. Of course, people exaggerate. My mother always told me to check the story with the person before I passed it on. That is the rule. Ask the source, then decide what to say.
